text:
The Consumer Board in exercise of powers vested under section 120 of the Consumer Protection Act of Bhutan 2012 hereby adopts the Consumer Protection Rules and Regulations 2015 (Revision) Regulations 2022.

Title

1. This Rules and Regulations shall be called the Consumer Protection Rules and Regulations 2015 (Revision) Regulations 2022

Commencement

2. This Rules and Regulations shall come into force on 21st April, 2022.

Revision

3. This Rules and Regulations shall revise Rule 53(b) of the Consumer Protection Rules and Regulations 2015.

PENALTIES

4. Rule 53 (b) of Consumer Protection Rules and Regulations 2015 is revised as:

“Rule 53(b)

Misleading Representation

(1) Any person who commits an offence of misleading representation under section 6 of Consumer Protection Act 2012 shall be liable to pay a fine equivalent to value of:

(a) goods sold; and/or

(b) goods displayed; and/or

(c) goods meant for sale.

(2) Any person who commits an offence of misleading representation under section 6 of Consumer Protection Act 2012 shall be liable to pay a fine equivalent to value of:

(a) services provided; and/or
(b) services indicated to the consumers.

(3) If a person commits an offence under section 6 of Consumer Protection Act 2012, and if the value of the goods or services cannot be determined, a fine equivalent to a national minimum wage rate of eight months shall be imposed.

Misleading indication of price

(4) Any person who commits offence of Misleading indication of price under section 7 and 8 of Consumer Protection Act 2012 shall be liable to pay a fine equivalent to value of:

(a) goods sold; and/or

(b) goods displayed; and/or

(c) goods meant for sale.

(5) Any person who commits offence of Misleading indication of price under section 7 and 8 of Consumer Protection Act 2012 shall be liable to pay a fine equivalent to value of:

a) services provided; and/or

(b) services indicated to the consumers.

(6) If a person commits an offence under section 7 and 8 of Consumer Protection Act 2012, and if the value of the goods or services cannot be determined, a fine equivalent to a national minimum wage rate of eight months shall be imposed.

Price tag

(7) Any person who commits offence of price tag under section 9 of Consumer Protection Act 2012 shall be liable to pay a fine equivalent to value of:

(a) goods sold; and/or
(b) goods displayed for sale.

(8) Any person who commits offence of price tag under section 9 of Consumer Protection Act 2012, wherever applicable, shall be liable to pay a fine equivalent to value of:

(a) services provided; and/or
(b) services indicated to the consumers.

(9) If a person commits an offence under section 9 of Consumer Protection Act 2012, and if the value of the goods or services cannot be determined, a fine equivalent to a national minimum wage rate of eight months shall be imposed.

Gifts, Prizes, Free Offers

(10) Any person who commits an offence of Gifts, Prizes, Free Offers under section 10 and 11 of the Consumer Protection Act 2012 shall be liable to pay a fine equivalent to a national minimum wage rate of two months;

Claim That Goods Are Limited

(11) Any person who commits an offence of claims that goods are limited under section 12 and 13 of the Consumer Protection Act 2012 shall be liable for a fine equivalent to 50% of value of goods sold or services provided through unfair trade practices or equivalent to a national minimum wage rate of eight months; if the value cannot be determined;

Demanding or Accepting Payment without Intending to Supply

(12) Any person who commits an offence of demanding or accepting payment without intending to supply under section 14 of the Consumer Protection Act 2012 shall be liable for a fine of 50% of the value of the goods or services or equivalent to a national minimum wage rate of eight months; if value cannot be determined;

Land and Building

(13) Any person who commits offence of land and building under section 15 of Consumer Protection Act 2012 shall be liable to pay a fine equivalent to value of goods sold or equivalent to a national minimum wage rate of eight months, if the value cannot be determined;

Misleading Advertising and Presumption of Liability for Advertisement

(14) Any person who commits an offence of misleading advertising under section 16 and 17 of the Consumer Protection Act 2012 shall be liable for a fine of 50% of the value of goods or services through misleading advertisement or equivalent to a national minimum wage rate of eight months; if the value cannot be determined.

Non - discrimination of goods and services

(15) Any person who commits offence of discrimination under section 18 of Consumer Protection Act 2012 shall be liable to pay a fine equivalent to value of:

(a) goods sold; and/or

(b) goods displayed for sale; and/or

(c) goods meant for sale.

(16) Any person who commits offence of discrimination under section 18 of Consumer Protection Act 2012 shall be liable to pay a fine equivalent to value of:

(a) services provided; and/or

(b) services indicated to the consumers.

(17) If a person commits an offence under section 18 of Consumer Protection Act 2012, and if the value of the goods or services cannot be determined, a fine equivalent to a national minimum wage rate of eight months shall be imposed.

(18) For any other offence which is not covered above, the penalty shall be

(a) 50% of the value of the goods or services where the value can be determined; or

(b) Equivalent to a national minimum wage rate of eight months; where the value of the goods or services cannot be determined.

Definition

In the Consumer Protection Rules and Regulations 2015, after Rule 168 (a), new rule 168 is inserted as

(aa) “National Minimum Wage Rate” means national minimum wage rate approved by the Royal Government of Bhutan from time to time”.

(bb) “Gifts, Prizes, Free Offers” refers to any incentives or benefits offered by the business entities to the consumer as part of their product /service or business promotion, on purchase of a particular product/service, without any additional charges.
